The midterm elections have put Democrats in control

At least six people have been killed
and more than a dozen wounded
after a man opened fire in downtown Krakow, Poland.
Terry Schultz reports the suspect
is a 24-year-old Polish man
who was shot and wounded by police.
- Authorities say the man fired an automatic rifle
from a car driven into the main market square
of Poland's second largest city before being apprehended.
Three people were found dead at the home of the gunman
two hours away from Krakow.
In a press conference, Polish government officials said
it appears the gunman was influenced by far-right ideology.
During the shooting, he wore military-style camouflage
and a helmet and was carrying a large amount
of ammunition and weapons in his car.
Four of the dead are women and one victim is from the UK.
At least 15 others were injured.
European Union foreign policy chief, Kaya Kalas, says,
"The tragic loss of life in the shooting in Krakow
is a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland."
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
- A promising new drug used to lower the risk
of heart attacks and strokes has failed its first big test.
NPR's Rob Stein has the story.
- Researchers tested an experimental drug
that can cut levels of a cholesterol-carrying particle
in the blood known as lipoprotein A or LP little A.
The protein has long been associated
with an increased risk for heart attacks and strokes.
But in a study involving more than 8,000 heart disease
patients, the drug, called pellacarsin,
failed to reduce the risk for cardiovascular complications.
The failure stunned heart specialists
who had hoped drugs like this would provide
the next big advance in preventing heart disease.
But many experts say the approach may still work
using other drugs or treating patients
perhaps either longer or sooner.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
- This is NPR.

- Zoo Atlanta has two new residents.
They are giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang.
They arrived from China in September,
but they just got to make their public debut on Friday.
The zoo waited for their public appearance
in order to give the pandas some time
to get used to their new surroundings.
The six-year-old pandas are part
of a 10-year loan agreement with China
and marks the return of pandas to the zoo
after a two-year absence.
Zoo Atlanta is now one of three U.S. zoos
that house pandas and are part of what is described
as China's global panda diplomacy.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
